title: Payment Arrangements Servicing Sheet — The Restructured Installment
content:
When a plan under Payment Arrangements is restructured, the new regular installment is worked out as follows.

## Definition

The restructure keeps the plan's schedule anchor installment as the first restructured installment and re-spreads the restructure balance evenly over the restructured count.

The restructured installment is the restructure balance divided by the restructured count, rounded up to the type's rounding unit; it is never below the type's minimum installment for the plan's frequency nor below the type's monthly-equivalent minimum percentage of the restructure balance, measured as a monthly equivalent.

The base count is the plan's installment count less its schedule anchor installment, the regular installments still to fall due from the anchor on. The restructured count is the base count plus the hardship relief, plus the tenure credit, plus the relief-credit bonus, less the missed-entry penalty and less the returned-debit penalty, and never more than the type's largest installment count less the schedule anchor installment.

The restructure balance is the plan's whole arrangement balance, and the hardship relief, the tenure credit, the relief-credit bonus and both penalties are 0 installments, so the restructured count is the base count.

## How the amount is fixed

The restructured installment is the highest of three amounts, stated to the cent:

1. the restructure balance divided by the restructured count (a count below one being taken as one), rounded up to the type's rounding unit;
2. the type's minimum installment for the plan's frequency (weekly, biweekly or monthly minimum);
3. the percentage floor: the type's monthly-equivalent minimum percentage of the restructure balance, multiplied by 12 and divided by the periods per year of the plan's frequency (52 weekly, 26 biweekly, 12 monthly), rounded up to the type's rounding unit.

The cap on the count is applied before the division. The rounding unit, the frequency minimums, the monthly-equivalent minimum percentage and the largest installment count are product figures of the arrangement type.

## Worked figures (hypothetical inputs; type figures for the illustration: monthly minimum 75.00, monthly-equivalent minimum 4.0 percent, rounding unit 1.00, largest count 24)

A monthly plan with an installment count of 24 and schedule anchor installment 10; arrangement balance 2100.00.

- Base count: 24 less 10 is 14. Cap: 24 less 10 is 14. Restructured count: 14.
- Spread: 2100.00 divided by 14 is 150.00.
- Percentage floor: 4.0 percent of 2100.00 is 84.00, multiplied by 12 and divided by 12 is 84.00.
- Highest of 150.00, 75.00 and 84.00: the restructured installment is 150.00.

With an arrangement balance of 1000.00 instead: 1000.00 divided by 14 is 71.43, rounded up to 72.00; the percentage floor is 40.00; the frequency minimum of 75.00 is the highest, so the restructured installment is 75.00.

On a biweekly plan, a restructure balance of 2600.00 and a 4.0 percent minimum give 104.00 per month, multiplied by 12 and divided by 26: a percentage floor of 48.00.
